andromeda: Princess chained to a rock for a sea monster; contains our nearest large galaxy
antlia: Faint southern constellation named after a vacuum pump by Lacaille
apus: Constellation near the south celestial pole named after a colourful New Guinea bird
aquarius: Zodiac constellation of a figure pouring from a jar
aquila: Its brightest star is Altair; the bird that carried Zeus's thunderbolts
ara: Southern constellation of a sacrificial table where the gods swore an oath
aries: Zodiac constellation of the golden-fleeced animal Jason sought
auriga: Its brightest star is Capella; a figure driving horses
bootes: Its brightest star is Arcturus; a figure driving the bears
caelum: One of the faintest constellations, Lacaille's engraving tool
camelopardalis: Large faint northern constellation named after a long-necked animal
cancer: Zodiac constellation home of the Beehive Cluster; a clawed creature
canes-venatici: A pair of hounds near the Big Dipper's handle
canis-major: Contains Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky
canis-minor: Its brightest star is Procyon; Orion's smaller hound
capricornus: Zodiac constellation of a creature half goat, half fish
carina: Contains Canopus, the second-brightest star; part of the ship Argo
cassiopeia: W-shaped constellation of a vain queen
centaurus: Contains Alpha Centauri, the closest star system to the Sun
cepheus: King of Ethiopia, husband of the W-shaped queen
cetus: The sea monster sent to devour a chained princess
chamaeleon: Small constellation near the south pole named after a colour-changing reptile
circinus: Small southern constellation of a tool for drawing circles
columba: Constellation of the bird Noah released from the ark
coma-berenices: Named after an Egyptian queen who sacrificed her locks
corona-australis: Semicircle of stars at the archer's feet in the southern sky
corona-borealis: Semicircle of stars said to be Ariadne's wedding crown
corvus: Small four-star constellation of Apollo's black bird
crater: Constellation of Apollo's goblet, next to the black bird
crux: The smallest constellation, pictured on the Australian flag
cygnus: Contains Deneb; the bird Zeus became to visit Leda
delphinus: Small diamond of stars; the sea mammal that rescued Arion
draco: Long beast coiling around the north celestial pole, guardian of golden apples
eridanus: Long winding constellation that ends at the bright star Achernar
fornax: Lacaille's chemical oven; home of a famous Hubble deep field
gemini: Zodiac constellation with the stars Castor and Pollux
grus: Southern constellation named after a long-legged wading bird
hercules: Contains the great globular cluster M13; named after the strongest hero
hydra: The largest constellation, a many-headed water monster
hydrus: A small male water monster near the Magellanic Clouds
indus: Faint southern constellation representing a Native American figure
lacerta: Small zigzag of stars in the north named after a reptile
leo: Zodiac constellation with Regulus; the Nemean beast
leo-minor: Small faint constellation just north of a zodiac big cat
lepus: Constellation of an animal crouching at Orion's feet
libra: The only zodiac constellation that isn't a living creature: a balance
lupus: A wild canine in the southern Milky Way
lynx: Faint northern constellation said to need sharp, cat-like eyes to see
mensa: The faintest constellation, named after a flat-topped mountain in Cape Town
microscopium: Lacaille's instrument for seeing tiny things
monoceros: Faint constellation of a one-horned horse
musca: Small southern constellation named after an insect
norma: Lacaille's carpenter's tool for right angles
octans: Contains the south celestial pole; a navigation instrument
ophiuchus: The "13th" constellation the Sun passes through; a healer holding a snake
orion: Famous three-star belt between Betelgeuse and Rigel
pavo: Southern constellation of a bird with a showy tail
pegasus: Winged horse with a Great Square of stars
perseus: The hero who slew Medusa; home of a famous August meteor shower
phoenix: Southern constellation of a firebird reborn from ashes
pisces: The last zodiac constellation, two creatures tied by a cord
puppis: The rear section of the ship Argo, its largest piece
pyxis: Small constellation of a ship's magnetic navigation instrument
reticulum: Small southern constellation named after a crosshair grid
sagitta: The third-smallest constellation, a projectile shot from a bow
sagittarius: Zodiac constellation pointing toward the galaxy's centre, with a "Teapot" asterism
scorpius: Zodiac constellation whose red heart is Antares
sculptor: Home of the galactic south pole; an artist's studio
scutum: Small constellation with the Wild Duck Cluster; a soldier's defence
serpens: The only constellation split into two parts
sextans: Faint constellation of an instrument for measuring star angles
taurus: Zodiac constellation with the Pleiades and Aldebaran
telescopium: Faint southern constellation named after an astronomer's tool
triangulum: Small three-star constellation with a nearby spiral galaxy, M33
triangulum-australe: Three bright stars forming a shape in the far southern sky
tucana: Contains the Small Magellanic Cloud; a big-beaked bird
ursa-major: Large northern constellation whose seven brightest stars form a ladle
vela: The part of the ship Argo that caught the wind; home of a famous pulsar
virgo: Zodiac constellation whose brightest star is Spica
volans: Southern constellation of a fish that glides above the waves
vulpecula: Faint constellation of a small wild canine, home of the Dumbbell Nebula
